definitions.explanation: A written order from a doctor specifying medicine to be dispensed by a pharmacist. In Japan, prescriptions are typically taken to a separate pharmacy rather than filled at the hospital.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}に{処方箋|しょほうせん}を{書|か}いてもらった。
examples.english: The doctor wrote me a prescription.

examples.japanese: {処方箋|しょほうせん}を{薬局|やっきょく}に{持|も}っていく。
examples.english: I take the prescription to the pharmacy.

examples.japanese: {処方箋|しょほうせん}なしでは{買|か}えない{薬|くすり}もある。
examples.english: Some medicines cannot be bought without a prescription.

examples.japanese: {処方箋|しょほうせん}の{有効期限|ゆうこうきげん}は4{日間|かかん}です。

notes:
COMPOSITION: {処方|しょほう} (formulation, prescription) + {箋|せん} (slip, tag)

JAPANESE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM:
In Japan, clinics and hospitals usually do not dispense medicine directly. Instead, patients receive a {処方箋|しょほうせん} and take it to a nearby {調剤薬局|ちょうざいやっきょく} (dispensing pharmacy).

KEY TERMS:
・{処方箋|しょほうせん}{薬|やく} - prescription medicine
・{市販薬|しはんやく}/{OTC{薬|やく}} - over-the-counter medicine
・{調剤薬局|ちょうざいやっきょく} - dispensing pharmacy
・{院内処方|いんないしょほう} - in-hospital dispensing
・{院外処方|いんがいしょほう} - out-of-hospital dispensing

VALIDITY: Prescriptions in Japan expire after 4 days (including the day of issue), so they must be filled promptly.

COMMON VERBS:
・{処方箋|しょほうせん}を{書|か}く - to write a prescription
・{処方箋|しょほうせん}を{出|だ}す - to issue a prescription
・{処方箋|しょほうせん}を{持|も}っていく - to take a prescription (to the pharmacy)
